cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Before I book the trip, who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Whose objection would stop you paying the deposit?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's. But she's away, and her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the deputy release it alone, or does she still need the treasurer's permission?

mechanism: A copies apparent decision-making confidence, learns it is not authority, and probes each correction to locate real veto power without admitting confusion.
confusable: D67 hierarchy procedure is not enough; D54 tests who can actually approve or reverse.
comparison: Trip deposit versus funding a leaking-pipe repair.
seedUse: Preserve follow-up questions about deputy powers and caretaker influence; avoid generic authority speeches.
